subject: Incremental workload top-up, trial option, and per-token commit structure
messages:
From: Elliot Garner <elliot@serene-retail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Scaling per-token credits for new personalization workloads

Hi Tessa,

Quick background: our personalization team is launching a new product line that will spike generation and embedding volume. Rough estimate is ~150B tokens/mo in steady state across two new features (session-based personalization + nightly re-runs). We want to understand how Redwood handles incremental usage-based discounts and whether we can layer a short-term onboarding commit before committing to a longer-term tier.

Questions:
- Can we top up tokens on top of our existing contract (current committed tier covers core chat), and how are overages credited vs billed?
- If we commit an incremental monthly credit (e.g., 100B tokens) for 3 months as a trial, can that convert to a 12-month commit with backdated pricing?
- Any constraints around burst capacity for realtime features and how that affects effective per-token rate?

Target timeline: pilot in Jan, full production in Mar if pricing and SLA align. Happy to share telemetry and estimated token mix if helpful.

Thanks,
Elliot
Head of Product, Serene Retail
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Garner <elliot@serene-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Scaling per-token credits for new personalization workloads

Elliot — thanks for the context, and congrats on the product launch roadmap. High level guidance below; I attached our latest price sheet (redwood_price_sheet_v3.pdf) and a draft SOW to speed alignment.

Short answers up front:
- Yes, we can do an incremental commit (top-up) layered on your existing hosted API contract.
- We support a 3-month pilot commit that can optionally convert to a 12-month term; conversion rules (pricing, retroactive credits) depend on commitment size and billing cadence.
- Burst capacity can be included as a separate reserved burst bucket; we size it to your P95 QPS profile. Burst inclusion slightly changes the effective unit price but provides a guaranteed headroom SLA.

Proposed commercial path (starter):
- 3-month pilot: purchase 100B token credits (monthly allotment) for 3 months. Credits drawn FIFO against the pilot pool.
- Conversion option: if Serene converts to 12-month commitment within the pilot window, we'll apply a conversion rebate that reduces pilot effective rate to the 12-month committed rate for all pilot usage (i.e., retroactive reconciliation).
- Pricing examples (illustrative): baseline hosted rate = $X per 1k tokens; pilot commit effective = baseline * 0.88; 12-month commit effective = baseline * 0.72. Exact $/1k will depend on token mix (embed vs gen) and whether burst reserve is purchased.

Next steps I recommend: 1) confirm desired pilot size (100B vs 150B), 2) confirm whether you want burst reserve, 3) sign the short order form so we can provision credits and burst pool.

I copied Ben and Monica to help with capacity and rollout, and Lauren for billing/finance terms.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On attachments: redwood_price_sheet_v3.pdf (line-item banding and sample math), SOW-draft.docx (onboarding plan and success milestones).

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Scaling per-token credits for new personalization workloads — finance input requested

Ben,

We can approve with these guardrails:
- Minimum monthly convertible commit must be $100,000 (so 100B at pilot pricing needs to meet that floor; if not, use scaled pricing).
- 12-month conversion requires invoice schedule net-30 and an upfront initial month payment on conversion.
- Rollover: unused pilot credits may roll forward up to 90 days, but not beyond the converted 12-month window.
- Legal must review the Docusign order form and SOW; no changes to standard refund policy without exec sign-off.

If the customer also adds a second product/team within 90 days of conversion, we can layer an additional 5% off the committed rate (stackable), subject to a consolidated minimum commit across both teams.

I'll need expected dollar volumes to validate margin — add those and I'll give a final approval.

Thanks,
Lauren
VP, Finance — Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Garner <elliot@serene-retail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Incremental workload top-up, trial option, and per-token commit structure

Elliot — thanks, we've aligned internally and here's a consolidated proposal for your pilot -> conversion path. Posting as bullets to keep it actionable.

Proposal summary:
- Pilot: 3 months, 100B token credits per month. Pilot effective rate = baseline * 0.88 (illustrative).
- Conversion option: Convert to a 12-month committed contract any time during pilot. On conversion we will: 1) apply a conversion rebate so pilot usage is retroactively billed at the 12-month committed effective rate, and 2) set monthly committed credit to the agreed committed quantity.
- Minimums & billing: convertible pilot must meet $100,000/month floor to be eligible; invoices net-30; initial invoice on conversion due up front for month 1.
- Rollover & burst: unused pilot credits roll up to 90 days. Add optional burst reserve (sized to P95) for guaranteed headroom; burst reserve is a separate monthly fee.
- Expansion incentive: if Serene adds another team/product within 90 days of conversion, Redwood will add a 5% stackable discount on the committed effective rate (subject to consolidated min commit).

Files: attached SOW-draft.docx and redwood_price_sheet_v3.pdf. I also dropped an order form into DocuSign to speed things up: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/put-order-form-here

If that looks good I'll pull Legal for a quick review and send a clean order form. Target provisioning timeline: credits and burst reserve available within 3 business days after signed order.

Next actions for Serene: 1) confirm pilot size (100B vs 150B), 2) indicate whether you want burst reserve, 3) confirm whether you want the expansion incentive tied to additional teams.

Best,
Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Tessa — thank you, that level of clarity is helpful. Quick responses:

1) We'd like to start with the 3-month 100B pilot, but propose the following amendment: allow the pilot to run as a paid trial with the option to convert to 12 months at any point and apply the conversion rebate as you described. If after 3 months we convert, we expect retroactive pricing to apply to pilot months.

2) We want to try the pilot without the burst reserve initially; if we hit latency issues we'll add it in month 2.

3) We agree to the $100k/month floor if your final price math supports it. One ask: if we add another team within 90 days and qualify for the 5% stacking incentive, can we have that written into the order form to avoid later renegotiation?

If you can update the DocuSign to explicitly note the conversion rebate and the 90-day expansion incentive, we can sign the pilot order this week and start provisioning in early Jan.

Thanks — Elliot
